thesis: The 3.9x volume signal does not yet have a fresh operating result behind it, while fiscal Q1 2027 results are a binary event scheduled for September 9. Fiscal 2026 ended with 8.0% fourth-quarter rental-revenue growth, $2.055 billion of free cash flow, repurchases and ample facility availability, but fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA margin fell 290 basis points on the issuer's normalized comparison. Those positives do not justify a new entry before the report because the company also completed a debt-classification restatement tied to a material weakness, and a subsidiary is in active litigation with a September 8 joinder deadline; both risk flags mechanically force low conviction.
invalidation: Reassess after September 9 if rental-revenue growth remains within or above the issuer's 5%-8% fiscal 2027 outlook, adjusted EBITDA-margin pressure materially narrows on a comparable basis, guidance is maintained or raised, and no new control weakness is disclosed.
sources: Sunbelt Rentals fiscal Q1 2027 event announcement: https://ir.sunbeltrentals.com/news-events/press-releases
Philadelphia Indemnity Insurance Company v. Sunbelt Rentals docket: https://dockets.justia.com/docket/washington/wawdce/2%3A2026cv01956/363774

thesis: Samsara's confirmed fiscal Q2 2027 release supports a long: revenue and ending ARR each grew 30% year over year, net new ARR grew 28%, issuer-reported basic and diluted EPS was $0.03, operating cash flow was positive, and full-year revenue guidance increased. The strongest counter-evidence is that Q3 revenue-growth guidance slows to 24% and non-GAAP operating-margin guidance excludes potentially material stock-compensation expense; this does not overturn the positive read because full-year guidance rose and ARR growth remained durable. Motive's active case has a court-scheduled November 14 expert-discovery deadline, so active_litigation mechanically forces low conviction.
invalidation: Invalidate the long if Samsara lowers the fiscal 2027 revenue floor below $2.043 billion, withdraws its U.S.-GAAP-profitable outlook, or reports ARR growth below 25% year over year at the next release.
sources: Samsara SEC-filed Q2 fiscal 2027 earnings release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1642896/000162828026060438/samsaraepr-q22027.htm
Motive Technologies v. Samsara case schedule: https://ipverse.greyb.com/litigations/motive-technologies-inc-v-samsara-inc--cand--3-24-cv-00902

thesis: Guidewire's confirmed fiscal 2026 results were strong, but the fiscal 2027 revenue outlook midpoint implies roughly 16% growth after 23% growth in fiscal 2026, and the fiscal Q1 revenue range points to slower near-term conversion; the sharp, high-volume repricing therefore supports avoiding a new entry until conversion evidence improves. The strongest counter-evidence is 19% ARR growth, 22% fully ramped ARR growth, record sales activity, low gross attrition and higher operating-cash-flow guidance. Those strengths do not reverse the avoid read because the immediate company outlook itself shows a slower realization path after elevated expectations. King v. Guidewire remains active with a court-scheduled October 6 mediation hearing, so active_litigation mechanically forces low conviction.
invalidation: Reverse the avoid thesis if a subsequent issuer report shows fiscal Q1 revenue above the $378 million guidance ceiling, raises fiscal 2027 ending ARR above $1.460 billion, supplies evidence that backlog-to-ARR conversion has reaccelerated, and the scheduled mediation produces no material escalation.
sources: Guidewire fiscal Q4 and fiscal 2026 earnings release: https://guidewire.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/guidewire-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026

thesis: Docusign's confirmed fiscal Q2 2027 release supports a long: revenue grew 9%, Intelligent Agreement Management expanded to 15.1% of ARR from 12.6% one quarter earlier, issuer-reported gross margin improved, diluted EPS increased year over year, and management raised full-year revenue and ARR expectations. The strongest counter-evidence is that about 1.3 percentage points of revenue growth came from foreign exchange and non-GAAP gross margin declined slightly year over year; it does not overturn the read because IAM mix and the raised company outlook improved together. Hart v. Docusign remains active with a September 15 case-management conference on the latest public docket despite a magistrate's dismissal recommendation, so active_litigation mechanically forces low conviction.
invalidation: Invalidate the long if Docusign cuts fiscal 2027 ARR growth below 8.5%, lowers its stated fiscal Q4 IAM share objective below 18%, or the district court rejects dismissal in Hart and the case develops into a material operating exposure.
sources: Docusign SEC-filed Q2 fiscal 2027 earnings release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1261333/000126133326000088/q227ex-991er.htm

thesis: Victoria's Secret's confirmed Q2 2026 release showed 10% net-sales growth, 9% comparable-sales growth, adjusted operating income of $124 million excluding the tariff-refund benefit, and higher full-year sales and adjusted operating-income guidance. The strongest positive counter to an avoid is that this is credible turnaround evidence rather than a purely technical move. It does not resolve the entry case because fiscal Q3 operating-income guidance is only $10-$20 million while management is increasing marketing investment and still navigating tariff uncertainty, leaving the durability of the Q2 step-up unsettled. A brand-management affiliate faces an active TCPA case with a September 15 case-management conference, so active_litigation mechanically forces low conviction.
invalidation: Invalidate the avoid if fiscal Q3 reported operating income exceeds the issuer's $20 million guidance ceiling, sales meet or exceed the $1.600 billion guidance ceiling, full-year adjusted operating-income guidance rises again, and the September litigation conference produces no material escalation.
sources: Victoria's Secret SEC-filed Q2 2026 earnings release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1856437/000185643726000019/ex991vsxyq22026earningsrel.htm
Minter v. Victoria's Secret Direct Brand Management public docket: https://dockets.justia.com/docket/california/candce/4%3A2026cv04654/470288
